title: The silent-undo scan refuses a one-sentence in-place rewrite of a line as a dropped line, so an honest edit needs a Drops-lines trailer and a new head
why: Sighting 06:33 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 06:32, relayed from runner 11; the coordinator did not read the guard record, and triage has not; unproven): degen #706, `merge 706 --confirm` refused by the silent-undo scan at merge 3208dcca7. The scan reads a one-sentence in-place rewrite of the merge-grant line in the degen project instructions (CLAUDE.md) as a dropped line. Runner 11's read: the diff against main is only the intended sentence. The printed remedy is a commit with the trailer `Drops-lines: CLAUDE.md -- <reason>`; lane child-ci-degen pushes it, which costs a new head (CI, fix check, record). Degen #706 stays held until that head's run is green; #704 and #710 wait for it. Why it matters: the root rule says to rewrite superseded text in place, so a scan that counts every in-place rewrite as a drop refuses honest edits; rate unknown (unmeasured). Related and not the same: step silent-undo-appended-negation (every original token survives, only a negation is appended; ready) and silent-undo-restored-line (done). First act of the lane: read the guard record and the scan, reproduce on the #706 diff, red then green, with a control that a real dropped line is still refused. A check change, so review round 3 applies.
